conclusion: Both actual GGUF workloads complete on the local RTX 5080 and in simulation. All six latency predictions underestimate the native engine medians; no universal prediction-accuracy claim is supported.
error_definition: signed_error_percent = (simulation_ns / native_engine_median_ns - 1) * 100; negative means latency is underestimated

scope.hardware: Local AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D / 128 GiB DDR5-5600 / NVIDIA RTX 5080
scope.simulation_export: Comparison exports omit repeated UI visualization and per-cohort cost/metadata objects. All compared request metrics, overall traffic summaries and batch boundaries are retained.

protocol.primary_reference: median of five native server engine timings
protocol.dispersion: observed minimum/maximum; not a confidence interval or p95 estimate

measurement_boundaries.simulation: engine_request_begin to first/last token; TPOT = (last - first) / 127
measurement_boundaries.native: llama-server prompt-processing timer through first-token sampling; prompt_ms + predicted_ms through last generated token; TPOT = predicted_ms / 127
measurement_boundaries.client: QPC perf_counter_ns before HTTP POST through first/last non-empty SSE content; retained separately in native JSON
measurement_boundaries.limitation: Native does not expose the simulator engine-admission timestamp. The server engine timing excludes client transport and pre-prompt admission; the boundaries are close for this warm single request but not proven identical.

logic_corrections: Automatic GPU ranks resolve attached physical GDDR/HBM as local backing, preserving the GPU memory phase and avoiding an invented second addressed transfer.
Inferred CPU/GPU KV backing uses the same local resolution while CIM without explicit backing retains the existing remote path.
Physical recurrent state is allocated by layer/rank/actual request owner; committed state persists across decode cohorts and speculative scratch uses separate generations.

The recurrent scan keeps T*S arithmetic, reads T rows and writes T*value-width activations; initial/final state traffic is accounted separately once per invocation, instead of allocating T full states.
Native client timestamp collection uses Windows QPC perf_counter_ns and excludes the empty final stop notification.

source_alignment.source: Same llama.cpp checkout used to build the native CUDA executable
source_alignment.configured_existing_paths: Explicit source-derived GET_ROWS embedding row access and F32 hidden activation storage; actual model GGUF binding qualified in both cases
source_alignment.default_source_availability: The repository default source/llama.cpp-semantic directory was unavailable; this comparison explicitly supplied the actual build-source contract.
source_alignment.gpu_and_gddr_timing_model: Existing blackwell_analytical_v1 GPU model and physical GDDR preset; no timing parameters fitted to these results

verification.both_native_formal_workloads: five completed samples each; 512 processed prompt tokens, zero reused tokens, 128 outputs

remaining_limits: Embedding row conversion/dequantization compute is not priced by the qualified storage contract.
GPU kernel efficiency, launch costs and GDDR behavior remain analytical estimates; this test does not isolate each contribution to total error.
Native sampling/host overhead and engine timing boundary differences are not an exact per-task match.
The 27B file is a qwen35 hybrid decoder with 64 executed backbone layers; 15 nextn tensors are excluded from execution in both paths because speculative decoding is disabled.
Only these two files on this RTX 5080 were compared to native inference; the earlier preset matrix is simulation coverage, not native validation of every combination.
Earlier zero numerical drift for the acceleration path means equivalence to the simulator reference; it does not imply zero native prediction error.
Host output and logits precision contracts are marked partial by both simulation reports; the native comparison does not validate these missing contracts.
